title: Maintaining Proper Drainage Slope for Self-Scouring Flow
description: Correct pitch on horizontal drainage piping is critical to achieving self-scouring flow velocity. A frequent installation error is assuming a steeper slope is always better. If horizontal drain pipe is sloped too steeply, liquid waste flows rapidly ahead of solid materials, leaving solids behind to accumulate and dry into persistent blockages. Conversely, insufficient slope causes flow velocity to drop below the threshold needed to carry debris. Plumbers must adhere strictly to local plumbing code slope requirements to ensure liquids and solids move together smoothly through the drainage system.

Maintaining Proper Drainage Slope for Self-Scouring Flow

Correct pitch on horizontal drainage piping is critical to achieving self-scouring flow velocity. A frequent installation error is assuming a steeper slope is always better. If horizontal drain pipe is sloped too steeply, liquid waste flows rapidly ahead of solid materials, leaving solids behind to accumulate and dry into persistent blockages. Conversely, insufficient slope causes flow velocity to drop below the threshold needed to carry debris. Plumbers must adhere strictly to local plumbing code slope requirements to ensure liquids and solids move together smoothly through the drainage system.
